title: Acadia rescue awards2
description: Coast Guard Commandant Adm. Thad Allen addresses Coast Guard crews and guests at an awards ceremony at the Coast Guard Sector Field Office in Southwest Harbor Friday, Nov. 13, 2009. The crews worked together to coordinate the Aug. 23, 2009, rescue at Acadia National Park, after seven people were overtaken by a large wave and pulled out to sea in the wake of an off-shore hurricane that produced waves up to 20 feet high. (U.S. Coast Guard/Petty Officer 2nd Class Etta Smith)

transcript.text: It doesn't take many operations like this, where you have the hand reaching down to the hand reaching up to inform you that you truly made the right decision to join the service and make it a career.

The people that are sitting behind you here today and the people that are standing over here that were part of this operation have made a decision to serve the public and serve a greater good than themselves.

And when they are out there on the water in the air doing their jobs and supporting of our search or rescue operations, they have one thing on their mind and that's mission execution and making sure that as many people can come back as we can make possible within the limits of our equipment and our capabilities and our competencies.
The country expects that when these situations occur that we will be there, it's our job to do that for you.
It's our great pleasure to do that and it's our honor and as a comment on the Coast Guard, it's my honor to be here today.
There are many jobs you can do in this world. I can't think of a better job than what I have right now at this time at this day and this place.
To be with you, to be here and to celebrate by this gathering that we care about humanity, it is part of our tradition and lore organizational DNA in the Coast Guard.
And these men are women are proud to serve and I'm doubly proud to lead them. Thank you very much.
